page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, alongside 446 GB of local SSD storage. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate mixed performance profiles. The processor supports AVX and AVX512F instructions, achieving an average PassMark CPU score of 6992.14 and an average extended instructions score of 5859.32. However, raw compute performance is generally modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 38.77 GB/sec, though large block write speeds reach an average tier of 35.61 GB/sec. For database workloads, Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 5.89 million operations per second, while PassMark database operations score in the bottom 25% at 2207.87.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and bundled 446 GB local SSD storage, the ecs.i1.2xlarge is positioned for workloads requiring persistent local storage and moderate compute resources. It is suitable for small-to-medium database hosting, basic web serving, and lightweight caching layers. However, its weak single-core performance and poor compression metrics make it less optimal for compute-heavy tasks or large-scale data processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a balanced resource density of memory and local SSD storage on legacy Intel Xeon hardware, making it a viable option for storage-centric workloads that do not demand high-frequency CPU performance.
